subject.title: [Feature]: Allow job-level model override for cron jobs using sessionTarget=main + payload.kind=systemEvent

question: Should OpenClaw support explicit provider/model overrides for main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs, and if so should the public contract be `payload.model`, top-level cron fields, or a dedicated `sessionOverride` block?
rationale: Current code treats system events as text-only main-session injections; changing that crosses provider routing, session state, cron persistence, UI/CLI behavior, and heartbeat semantics that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Design an explicit override contract
options.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and prove both wake modes cannot leak or corrupt session model state.

options.title: Keep systemEvent text-only
options.body: Document this path as unsupported for model selection and steer cheaper scheduled model calls to isolated, current, or custom-session `agentTurn` jobs.

options.title: Fold into broader cron schema work
options.body: Defer this to the broader cron schema and cost-control discussion so model, context, timeout, and spend semantics are decided together.

recommendation.title: Design an explicit override contract
recommendation.body: Add a public cron-owned provider/model override shape, validate it like isolated cron payload models, and prove both wake modes cannot leak or corrupt session model state.

likelyOwner.reason: The product-sensitive cron/session/provider boundary overlaps recent cron runtime and prior model-override merge history tied to this owner signal.
